name: Faraday
long_description:
Industrial enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected software and machines, with critical knowledge held by a few experienced employees. 

Faraday builds self-improving systems that take on this operational work. We connect to existing software and machines and build training and evaluation environments around each company’s workflows and data.

Continuous learning turns each company’s expertise into a compounding asset. Completed work, corrections, and employee feedback improve the agents, and those improvements carry into future jobs. The business preserves its knowledge while becoming more capable over time.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.
one_liner: Industrial AI coordinating humans, agents, and machines

launches.title: Faraday: company-specific AI and infrastructure that run manufacturing workflows end to end, from the back office to the shop floor.
launches.body:
Hi! [Oscar Rangel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/oscar-rangel) and I are building [**Faraday**](https://faradaycompute.com/)**: company-specific AI and infrastructure that run manufacturing workflows end to end, from the back office to the shop floor.**\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lPjsWKoKgVcS4hAmL3_9lGuSBhrsMq4\_](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lPjsWKoKgVcS4hAmL3_9lGuSBhrsMq4_/)

Manufacturing work spans disconnected systems, machines, spreadsheets, email, and tribal knowledge. Faraday connects them so agents can handle engineering reviews, quoting, production scheduling, inventory, sales, and accounts payable.

Each workflow adds knowledge and capabilities to a shared foundation that grows with the business. We build RL environments around each company’s processes and exceptions, helping agents improve through real-world outcomes and human corrections.

We work across industrials, from distributors and automotive suppliers to precision manufacturers.

**Our ask:** We’d love introductions to industrial leaders looking to grow without operations becoming the bottleneck. Building hardware? Let’s explore how we can shorten your suppliers’ lead times.

Special thanks to [@David Lieb](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/11216) and [@Max Kolysh](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5516) for believing in us and guiding us!
